introduction: Buddhism and Jainism emerged in the 6th century BCE as reform movements against the Vedic tradition. Both emphasized non-violence, renunciation, and moral living, but they also have important differences in their doctrines. At this level, we will understand their basic lives, teachings, and key events.

core_concepts.title: Life of Gautama Buddha
core_concepts.description: Gautama Buddha was born in Lumbini, attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, delivered his first sermon at Sarnath, and attained Mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar. He taught the Middle Path and the Four Noble Truths.

core_concepts.title: Life of Mahavira
core_concepts.description: Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. He was born in Kundagrama and attained Kevala Jnana after intense penance. He taught non-violence, truth, and non-possession.

core_concepts.title: Four Noble Truths
core_concepts.description: Buddha taught the Four Noble Truths - suffering, cause of suffering, cessation of suffering, and the path leading to its cessation. These form the foundation of Buddhism.

core_concepts.title: Triratna (Jainism)
core_concepts.description: In Jainism, the path to liberation is based on three jewels - Right Faith, Right Knowledge, and Right Conduct.

core_concepts.title: Principle of Non-Violence
core_concepts.description: Both religions emphasize non-violence, but Jainism follows it in a much stricter form, avoiding harm even to the smallest living beings.

important_entities.name: First Buddhist Council
important_entities.key_fact: Held at Rajagriha during Ajatashatru’s reign

important_entities.name: Second Buddhist Council
important_entities.significance: Differences arose within the Buddhist Sangha

important_entities.name: Gautama Buddha
important_entities.significance: Preached the Middle Path and Four Noble Truths

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often get confused: Buddhism follows the doctrine of no soul (Anatman), whereas Jainism accepts the existence of soul in all living beings.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Level of Non-Violence is Not Same
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Both religions emphasize non-violence, but Jainism follows it more strictly, while Buddhism advocates a balanced approach.
Rishabhanatha is considered the founder of Jainism, while Mahavira is the 24th Tirthankara. Gautama Buddha is the founder of Buddhism.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Lumbini birth, Bodh Gaya knowledge, Sarnath sermon, Kushinagar nirvana
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps remember the four major events of Buddha’s life in sequence.
A simple way to recall the Four Noble Truths.
Helps remember the three jewels of Jainism.

exam_strategy_tips: If the question mentions 'Middle Path' or 'Four Noble Truths', it refers to Buddhism.
If the question includes 'extreme non-violence' or 'Tirthankara', identify it with Jainism.
